newsitem.title: UK: Insurers must improve service to banks-underwriter.
newsitem.headline: Insurers must improve service to banks-underwriter.

text.p: Insurers should enhance their service to banks, but banks have a role to play by furnishing more information about the risks to be insured, an industry expert said on Wednesday.

"Our service needs to be enhanced. Response times could be better, but we also need more assistance from the assured," Lloyd's of London underwriter Rupert Villers told the Insurance Institute of London.

Banking clients who provide a detailed run-down of the operating risks they want insured get a better deal. Otherwise insurers tend to raise premiums when the nature of a risk is vague, Villers said at the IIL meeting.

His talk, entitled "How the insurance industry can provide a risk transfer to the banking industry when it does not understand that industry", was a response to a presentation a year ago by another speaker, Hazel Mack.
Insurers provide a wide range of services to the banking industry, insuring many of the sector's electronic systems against failure, and had a good understanding of the risks involved, Villers said.
However, he added that "our role is not to understand every transaction and process, but to understand the risk in the banking industry."
